title: Kafka Fundamentals
description: Understand Kafka architecture, brokers, topics, and partitions for high-throughput event streaming.

data.text: Apache Kafka is a distributed event streaming platform designed to handle high-throughput, fault-tolerant data pipelines. Unlike traditional message queues, Kafka treats messages as an immutable, append-only log. This log-centric design enables replay, parallel processing, and long-term retention of events.

A Kafka cluster consists of one or more **brokers** — servers that store messages and serve clients. Each broker manages a set of partitions across topics. Brokers form a cluster by registering with ZooKeeper (or using the newer KRaft mode) and replicate data for fault tolerance.

data.title: Key Components
items: **Broker** — A single Kafka server that stores partitions and handles client requests.
**Topic** — A category or feed name to which messages are published (e.g., `orders`, `user-clicks`).
**Partition** — An ordered, immutable sequence of messages within a topic. Partitions enable parallelism.
**Producer** — Client that publishes messages to topics.
**Consumer** — Client that reads messages from topics.
**Consumer Group** — A group of consumers that share the work of consuming a topic.

data.definition:
flowchart TD
    P1[Producer] -->|writes| B1[Broker 1]
    P2[Producer] -->|writes| B2[Broker 2]
    P3[Producer] -->|writes| B1

    subgraph Kafka Cluster
        B1 -->|replicates| B2
        B2 -->|replicates| B1
        B1 -->|stores| T1[Topic: orders]
        B1 -->|stores| T2[Topic: events]
        T1 -->|partition 0| T1P0[Partition 0]
        T1 -->|partition 1| T1P1[Partition 1]
        T2 -->|partition 0| T2P0[Partition 0]
    end

    C1[Consumer Group A] -->|reads| B1
    C2[Consumer Group B] -->|reads| B2
data.caption: Kafka cluster with producers, brokers, topics, partitions, and consumer groups

data.text: Topics are the primary abstraction in Kafka. Each topic is divided into partitions, which are the unit of parallelism. Partitions are distributed across brokers. Messages within a partition are strictly ordered by offset — an incrementing integer. This ordering guarantee is critical for replay and stateful stream processing.

data.title: Partition Count Matters
data.text: Choose partition count carefully. More partitions increase throughput but also increase replication overhead and file descriptors. A common starting point is 3–6 partitions per topic for development, scaling up to hundreds for high-volume production topics.

terms.definition: A sequence ID for each message within a partition. Consumers track offsets to know where they left off.
The number of broker copies maintained for each partition. A factor of 3 means each partition lives on 3 brokers.
Brokers that are fully caught up with the partition leader and eligible to take over if the leader fails.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Kafka stores messages as an append-only log per partition.
Brokers form a cluster and replicate data for fault tolerance.
Topics are split into partitions for horizontal scaling.
Offsets provide message ordering within a partition.
data.takeaway: Kafka's partition-based log model is the foundation of its high throughput and durability guarantees.
